# by any test).
#
# source DLL:   plugins/1/plugin/menu.dll
# sha256:       ecc8eba384e2dd2bb7ada8655e63bd9a3962b899dbe4fd8efdf6e1734603a49a
# also seen:    plugins/4/plugin/menu.dll (identical surface and registration
#               sequence at different addresses: V2Link @ 0x10003500,
#               class builder FUN_10007510 @ 0x10007510)
#               sha256 a697b99271fe318751676ffd213b422b511d976c305f3a46082b618b9b08365e
# extraction:   plugins/analysis/run_pipeline.sh (Ghidra ExportNcbSurface +
#               DecompileCandidates + ncb_surface.py); report
#               plugins/analysis/menu-ecc8eba384e2.md
# registration: V2Link @ 0x10003570 (calls FUN_100075a0 and installs the
#               MenuItem global; also attaches the read-only Window.menu
#               property to the Window class);
#               FUN_100075a0 @ 0x100075a0 builds tTJSNativeClassForPlugin("MenuItem")
#               and registers every member below through TJSNativeClassRegisterNCM
#               (call site DAT_1001fba4, type 1 = method, type 2 = property,
#               property flag 0x10000 = static);
#               V2Unlink @ 0x10003b50 removes the global.
#
# The test `menu_dll_surface` compares the live VM surface for `MenuItem` with
# this list. One line per member, `<kind> <name>`, kind one of
# `method` / `ctor` / `property`; comment and blank lines are ignored.
#
# The recovered surface does not record method-vs-read-only-property: the
# pipeline puts read-only properties in the methods column because their
# registration call has the same arity as a method. The kind here follows the
# decompiled registration site (type 1 = method, type 2 = property), so it is
# not the pipeline's classification alone.
